key.description: Ticket ID prefix, e.g. STO. Uppercase letters and digits only, must start with a letter, 2-10 characters. Used to extract numeric IDs from branch names and tickets.

name.description: Short project name used in the worktree prefix template.

typeProperty.description: Property name holding the ticket type. Plugin tolerates either Select or Multi-Select on the live DB; when Multi-Select, it reads the first value and writes a single-item array.

prProperty.description: Property name (URL) where /notion-dev:ticket writes the PR link. When absent from the live DB, the plugin skips the write with a warning rather than aborting.

assigneeProperty.description: People property that create-task assigns new tickets to. Absence-tolerant — when missing or not People-typed on the live DB, the assignment write is skipped with a warning rather than aborting.

defaultAssignee.description: Default assignee for new tickets: a Notion user id, email, or display name, resolved via notion-get-users at create time. Empty string or absent means create-task prompts interactively. Written explicitly by /notion-dev:init (including "" when the user declines a default).

statusMap.description: Maps logical statuses to Notion option names. The plugin WRITES inProgress and implemented. It only READS done and cancelled — these exist so the epic-close check knows which of your Status options mean resolved, and no plugin command ever transitions a ticket into them. Defaults: inProgress→In Progress, implemented→Implemented, done→Done, cancelled→Cancelled.

typeMap.description: Maps logical type keys (feature, bug, improvement, research) to Notion option labels. Defaults: feature→Feature, bug→Bug, improvement→Improvement, research→Research.

staticProperties.description: Extra Notion properties to set on every new ticket. Keyed by property name; value is the option name (for Select/Status) or text value. Set once at ticket creation; never modified by updateTicket or upsertSection.

epicProperty.description: Select property holding the Epic tag in multi-task missions. Absence-tolerant — writes skip with a warning if the live DB has no such property.

phaseProperty.description: Select property holding the Phase tag when a mission groups tasks into sequential stages. Absence-tolerant.

stepProperty.description: Number property holding the sequence position within a Phase. Absence-tolerant.

creationDateProperty.description: Property holding the ticket's creation timestamp. The live property may be either a Date property (the plugin writes the creation timestamp) or a Created time property (Notion auto-populates; the plugin never writes). Absence-tolerant — when missing or of any other type, the write is skipped with a warning rather than aborting.

parentTaskProperty.description: Self-referential Relation property linking a ticket to its Epic container page. The only relation property this plugin configures — blocking order between tickets is not a relation, it is rendered into the ticket body as a '## Blocked by' section. Not because self-referential relations are symmetric (they are not), and not because subtype is undetectable (the propertyUrl field reveals it), but as a design judgment: the signal is asymmetric (absent proves single_property and safe; present is ambiguous, since a two-way relation whose companion was deleted still carries propertyUrl yet behaves one-way), and representing dependency order conditionally on that schema accident is worse than representing it uniformly in the body. Absence-tolerant, and type-tolerant on the same terms: a property of this name that exists but is not a self-referential Relation is treated exactly as if it were absent — fetchTicket returns "" for it, and no operation writes to or filters on it. Both unusable states are recorded (missing-property:parentTaskProperty / wrong-type:parentTaskProperty) and both degrade identically: containment falls back to Epic-select tagging and a marked epic can still be identified, but it can never gain children. /notion-dev:init detects a wrong-typed column under the default name and reports the Parent task slot unavailable when no correctly-typed relation could be bound at all; if it binds a differently-named self-referential relation instead, the slot is available and the mistyped column is reported as a note.

epicMarkerProperty.description: Checkbox property that marks a page as an Epic container. This is the sole signal used to identify epics — carrying an Epic select value or having children never enters into it. Set to true by createEpic (through createTicket's isEpic argument). The property is usable only when it is both present AND a checkbox type, and the two unusable states — absent, or present but not a Checkbox — degrade identically: epics cannot be identified at all, findEpics returns null, every guard treats the page as not an epic rather than falling back to any structural guess, and no operation ever queries or writes the property. Note findEpics also returns null when parentTaskProperty is unusable — epic containers need both slots, so discovery must not report finding a container that cannot take children. Both unusable states are recorded (missing-property:epicMarkerProperty / wrong-type:epicMarkerProperty). Read against the live schema by fetchTicket, findEpics and createEpic, each applying that check (and by createTicket only on its isEpic write path, which records nothing); read as an already-collapsed metadata value by getEpicContext, epic-update and /notion-dev:ticket's epic guard, which inherit it through fetchTicket. The full contract is stated once as the "Marker usability rule" under "Epic containers" in skills/ticket-system/references/create-ops.md.

prTargetBranch.description: PR target branch. Defaults to baseBranch when omitted.

preMergeChecks.description: Ordered list of skill names invoked before merge. Empty in simple flow.

postMergeHooks.description: Ordered list of skill names invoked after merge, as the last step of the cleanup phase — the primary checkout is on a freshly pulled base branch and the ticket worktree is already removed. Empty in simple flow.

dependencies.description: Optional setup-time hints. Current host skills, not these cached booleans, determine build-flow availability.

superpowers.description: Setup-time snapshot from /notion-dev:init. Not an availability gate; commands verify live superpowers skills.

featureDev.description: Setup-time snapshot from /notion-dev:init. Not an availability gate; commands verify live feature-dev skills.

prefix.description: Template for worktree dir name. Tokens: {name}, {key}, {id}.

dir.description: Directory, relative to the repo root, holding the OKF knowledge bundle notion-dev:knowledge reads and writes. The epic brief lives at <dir>/epic/<KEY>-<n>-<slug>.md.

retrieveBudget.description: --max-tokens passed to iwe retrieve: the bundle's share of a run's context.

warnBytes.description: Per-concept size above which knowledge.py check warns. Never fails.

extraTypes.description: Client-specific concept directories accepted beyond the canonical set.

python.description: The Python 3 interpreter every notion-dev command runs scripts/knowledge.py with — python3, python, or py -3. Written by /notion-dev:init from its probe; python3 stands for this value in every skill and command.

outputs.description: Generated evidence files to archive after this command. Paths resolve against the verification worktree; missing or non-regenerated files fail verification.

reviewer.description: Code reviewer the review-and-merge loop drives. 'codex' triggers via an @codex review comment; 'copilot' requests the copilot-pull-request-reviewer[bot] reviewer via the REST API. Either falls back to the local fresh-agent review loop when unavailable. Written by /notion-dev:init. When absent on an upgraded project, review-and-merge resolves a value for that run only (prompt, or default 'codex' non-interactively) and does not write the config; re-run /notion-dev:init to persist it.

reviewsCap.description: Maximum external review rounds on the lean path; default 3. Explicit positive values are honored. Independent internal review uses runtime full/delta budgets, not a second copy of this cap. Legacy workflows retain their documented 15-round default. Hand-edited: init and review do not rewrite this key. A cap never authorizes merging unmet mandatory work.

convergence.description: Hand-edited knobs that keep an epic converging. Init never prompts for them and preserves them on reconfigure, like reviewsCap.

nonGoalDestination.description: Where a filed follow-up with blocks_goal: no is created: backlog (no parent), related (no parent, linked from the epic's resolution entry) or epic:<KEY>-<n> (a standing debt epic). blocks_goal: yes follow-ups stay children of their epic.

rateWindow.description: Resolutions over which knowledge.py epic-goal computes FOLLOWUP_RATE.

rateThreshold.description: FOLLOWUP_RATE above which next-task recommends a re-scope pass instead of selecting another child.

fileThresholdLines.description: Filing criterion 3 (large enough to obscure review) needs more changed lines than this, or a second independent design question.

briefBudget.description: Line budget of an epic brief; over it, record prunes and links settled decisions to concepts before adding.

prBodyBudget.description: Characters above which workflow.py pr-body warns. Reasoning belongs in the knowledge capture.

failureModeClasses.description: The project's failure-mode classes for a design review of a new or changed contract surface (e.g. an HTTP service: client-acted verdicts, timeouts and concurrency, connection lifetime, upstream outage; a contract system: access control, re-entrancy, parameter bounds, storage/ABI compatibility). Wins over failureModeReference. Absent both, a neutral fallback list is used.

failureModeReference.description: Repo-relative path of a project file listing its failure-mode classes, one bullet per class. Read only at the design review (workflow.py failure-modes).

figureUnits.description: Extra units that make a number a quantitative PR-body claim, beside the generic built-ins (%, x, ms, s, minutes, days, bytes, tokens, lines, requests, calls). Add domain units (a currency, gas, bps) and counted nouns (tests).

generatedPaths.description: Glob or directory prefixes of generated files (lockfiles, codegen, exported API specs) that workflow.py changed-lines excludes from filing criterion 3's size.

match.description: Regex matched (full, case-insensitive) against a finding's labels, e.g. severity:(critical|high).

destinations.description: Ordered label -> destination rules for filed follow-ups; the first match wins over metaDestination and the blocks_goal routing. Use it so a finding that gates a launch or release keeps a parent instead of landing in the backlog. The plugin never interprets a label.

metaDestination.description: Where a follow-up labelled meta (tooling, CI, knowledge bundle, plugin) is filed: never under the product epic it was found in.

briefRetrieveShare.description: Share of knowledge.retrieveBudget the epic brief may use (estimated at 4 bytes per token). Over it, or over briefBudget lines, epic-goal reports brief.over_budget.
